answer: Every agent must own one security key, a USB stick costing about $25. Plugged in once, it creates a private key inside itself that never leaves the stick. Each epoch the agent touches the key so it signs a fresh challenge, and a signature from a copied file fails. One key serves one agent only, so a garden of fake accounts needs a real key per plant, while a plume of sign-ups at once stands out: a thousand keys cost $25,000 and take days to ship. The ripple is that each key needs a real computer, so one laptop cannot fake a thousand signatures in an hour.
